title: What One 10 kt Nuke Would Do to a US Carrier Group
description:
What would one nuclear bomb do to a US carrier group at sea?

A 10-kiloton nuclear burst, a 20-minute warning at best and a ring of ships that has 12 minutes to decide what it is looking at: this simulation follows the group ring by ring, then the hour after.

Half past midnight in the open Pacific, one nuclear weapon bursts beside a US carrier strike group. Nobody on the ships knows who fired it. What does a carrier group do in the first minute? Before the simulation we look at what is real: what a carrier group is, what the Navy learned when it tested nuclear bombs on ships at Bikini in 1946, and why the last tactical nuclear weapons left US ships in 1992.

This is a simulation. It has not happened. The attacker, the weapon and the position are fictional design choices, not predictions.

How this video was made: the narration is AI-generated (Google Text-to-Speech). Scenario segments are simulations built from published models and open sources; the attacker, the weapon, the ship formation, the position and the yield are ours, a scenario, not a forecast.
